purpose: Wow concepts for Phill's living card: a still plus a ~3 s clip each, shown on the Card Steering Board for Yes / Maybe / No.
approval: Phill, 22/10/2026, relayed by the coordinating session: generate with Higgsfield using existing credits only.

creditCap.rule: Read the Higgsfield balance first. Spend no more than 10% of it on this batch, and never more than 300 credits. Never buy credits or change the plan. One take per concept; a second take only if the first fails and the cap allows.
creditCap.estimate: About 25-60 credits per 3-5 s image-to-video take on DoP or Kling, so 4 ready concepts ≈ 100-240 credits. [INFERENCE from the Higgsfield research: 10-70 credits per take]

groundingRule: Every clip starts from a real input file below: the Unite Group logo from unite-group.in or a screenshot of the real card. No invented face for Phill; concepts that need him wait for his real photos. Generic hands and objects only, no identifiable people.
stillRule: The concept still is the clip's first frame, so no separate image generation is needed (saves credits).
output: Save each clip as wow/out/<id>.mp4 and its still as wow/out/<id>.jpg, upload both to the board artifact's assets, then set the option's video and image fields to the returned asset URLs.

concepts.title: The logo assembles from light
concepts.higgsfieldFeature: Image-to-video with a DoP Effects preset (particle build) on the real logo
concepts.model: Higgsfield DoP (or Kling 3.0 if DoP is unavailable)
concepts.prompt: Pitch-black background. Hundreds of tiny warm orange (#E55A2B) points of light drift in and lock together into exactly this logo, then a single soft orange pulse runs across it. The logo itself keeps its shape, lettering and original colour exactly as in the source image. No other text, no people.
concepts.whyItWows: The first second someone opens the card, the brand builds itself in their hand.

concepts.title: One card that isn't like the others
concepts.higgsfieldFeature: Image-to-video, Kling 3.0 with an Epic Camera Control crane pull-back
concepts.prompt: Start tight on this phone screen showing the glowing living card exactly as in the source image. The camera pulls back and up to reveal the phone lying on a table among dozens of plain, identical white paper business cards. Only the phone is lit, with a warm orange (#E55A2B) glow around it; the paper cards are flat and grey. No faces.
concepts.whyItWows: Phill's 'one donkey among the horses' idea in a single shot: everyone else hands out paper.

concepts.title: Tap, and the card comes alive
concepts.higgsfieldFeature: Image-to-video, DoP Basic Camera Control slow push-in with a tap moment
concepts.prompt: A hand holds a matte black NFC card against the top of this phone. On contact a ring of warm orange (#E55A2B) light ripples out from the card and the phone screen blooms into the living card shown in the source image. Slow push-in. Only a hand is visible, no face.
concepts.whyItWows: Shows the trade-show moment: no app, no typing, one tap.

concepts.title: Fly into the card
concepts.higgsfieldFeature: Image-to-video, DoP Epic Camera Control FPV push-through
concepts.prompt: The camera flies forward into the dark motion panel of this card, through the logo, into a deep space of soft warm orange (#E55A2B) light, as if the card opens into a world behind the screen. Keep the logo exactly as in the source. No people.
concepts.whyItWows: Turns a contact card into a doorway, which is where the game and the businesses live.

concepts.title: Phill looks up and says hello
concepts.blockedOn: A real head-and-shoulders photo of Phill and a 10-second voice memo in his own voice.
concepts.higgsfieldFeature: DoP push-in on his real portrait, then Lipsync Studio with his own recorded voice
concepts.whyItWows: The most personal opening a card can have, made from the real Phill.

concepts.title: Flip a ruined room back to new
concepts.blockedOn: Real before-and-after photos from a Disaster Recovery job, with the owner's permission to share.
concepts.higgsfieldFeature: Kling start-frame/end-frame transition between the real before and after photos
concepts.whyItWows: Proof of the work in three seconds; nothing sells restoration like a real before-and-after.
